- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.4), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- Sentiment +0.0 to +0.3 correlates with underestimation; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to ignore it; apply a 1–2% downward correction to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment as a volatility multiplier (e.g., +0.1 to +0.3 if sentiment > 0.2).
